data.question: Why does the verify-pack judge test see an empty reviewer log?

evidence.note: no retry or sleep: the cause (two writers) removed
hedge = 1 for the fake verifier; a single-call regression test

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test cannot detect the failure mode it is supposed to guard. The reported bug is a *truncation* race: with `hedge = 2`, the losing copy runs `printf ... > log`, which truncates the file **at redirect-open time**, and the copy is then killed **before it writes any bytes**, leaving the log empty. The new fake deliberately logs with append (`>>`), so in exactly that same interleaving — losing copy opens the file (no truncation) and is killed before its `printf` emits a byte — nothing is appended, `calls.txt` remains the winner's single `"x"`, and the assertion passes even though two hedged copies ran. The test only fails on the *other* interleaving, where the losing copy actually survives long enough to complete its write and yields `"xx"`, i.e. the interleaving in which the real bug does **not** manifest. Because the original bug was itself intermittent, this test will be flaky in the wrong direction (green on unfixed code) precisely when the hedged loser is cancelled inside the open→write window. A test that counts invocations must force each copy to complete a write (or have the loser record that it started, e.g. append before any truncating work / use a directory-per-copy marker) so that "two copies ran" is observable independent of the kill timing; as written, `hedge = 1` could be reverted and this test would still pass much of the time.
